purpose: README illustration of the proposed connector-to-business-plan architecture
prompt: Create a gorgeous, professionally art-directed architecture concept poster for the README of WorkspaceAlberta, an industrial AI workspace for real Canadian businesses. This is a polished editorial technology illustration, not a screenshot. Landscape 16:9, very high resolution, crisp fine typography and generous negative space. A deep midnight-ink background with restrained cream typography, copper-orange light, subtle pale teal accents, fine technical grid lines and beautiful dimensional glass/paper objects. Main headline in large, impeccably readable type at top left: "From business evidence to action." Small brand text above: "WORKSPACEALBERTA × JEV". Small capsule at top right: "ARCHITECTURE CONCEPT". Main composition flows left to right across the lower two thirds: four beautiful floating source tiles with simple custom line icons and the exact short labels "DOCUMENTS", "STRIPE", "EMAIL", "SOCIAL" converge as thin luminous copper lines into an elegant central decision lattice with a luminous node labeled "JEV" and small text "Typed judgments". The lattice contains a few branching paths, one selected orange path and quiet teal alternative paths, conveying evidence selection and decisions rather than text generation. The selected path feeds a sophisticated off-white stack of business-plan pages with subtle abstract charts, then a right-side organized action board with the label "BUSINESS PLAN" and small text "Evidence · Scenarios · Actions". Beneath the main flow, a fine understated process line with four concise labels: "CONNECT" → "UNDERSTAND" → "DECIDE" → "PLAN". The whole design should feel like a beautiful modern enterprise editorial poster: precise spacing, cinematic but subtle material lighting, restrained premium aesthetic, expert information hierarchy. No robots, no human faces, no stock AI brain, no fake metrics, no fake UI navigation, no claims of deployed connector support, no tiny illegible paragraphs. The only prominent orange should guide the eye through the decision path. Ensure every specified label is spelled exactly. The diagram is a future architecture concept, not a claim of currently implemented integrations.
